# Set Up an Alexa+ Routine to Automate Your Everyday Tasks

By the end of this guide you'll have a working Alexa Routine: you say one short phrase, and Alexa runs several things in a row — for example the news and then the weather. A routine is simply a saved list of steps that starts on its own when something happens (Amazon calls that something an **event**). No coding needed.

## Before you start
- An **Echo speaker**, **Echo Show**, or another Alexa device, plugged in and connected to your home Wi-Fi.
- The **Alexa app** on your phone or tablet, signed in with your Amazon account.
- Optional: smart-home devices (like smart bulbs or plugs) already added to the Alexa app, if you want the routine to control them.
- About **5–10 minutes**.

The menu names below come from Amazon's own help pages. The Alexa app changes often, so if a button looks a little different on your phone, look for the closest match.

## Step 1 — Open Routines in the Alexa app
Open the **Alexa** app. At the bottom of the screen, tap **More**, then tap **Routines**. This is where all your routines live, and where Amazon also offers ready-made ones under **Featured**. If you can't find More at the bottom, check whether your app needs an update in your phone's app store.
You'll know it worked when you see the Routines page, with or without routines already on it.

## Step 2 — Start a new routine
Tap the **+** in the top-right corner of the Routines page. A new, empty routine opens. If the app asks you for a name at any point, type something you'll recognize later, such as **Morning Wake-Up**.
You'll know it worked when you see an empty routine with a place to add an event and a place to add an action.

💬 Example: name it `Morning Wake-Up`.

## Step 3 — Choose what starts the routine
Tap **Add an event** and follow the steps in the app to choose what starts your routine. To start it with your voice, choose the option for a spoken phrase and type the words you'll say **after** the wake word — for example **good morning**. Don't type "Alexa" itself: the wake word is how you get Alexa's attention, the phrase is what comes after it. Keep the phrase short and unusual enough that you won't say it by accident.
You'll know it worked when your phrase appears as the event at the top of the routine.

💬 Example: type `good morning` as the phrase.

## Step 4 — Add the first action
Tap **Add an action** and follow the steps in the app. You'll see a list of things Alexa can do — Amazon's examples include playing the news, telling you the weather, reading out your calendar and controlling compatible smart-home devices. For this routine, pick the news. Some actions ask a follow-up question (for example which device should play it); answer it and continue.
You'll know it worked when the news appears as the first action in your routine.

## Step 5 — Add a custom action at the end
Tap **Add an action** again and look for the **custom action**. Amazon describes it like this: you can type in anything you can normally say to Alexa. Type **what's the weather today**. One rule from Amazon's help: a custom action has to be the **last** action in the routine, so add it after everything else.
You'll know it worked when your routine lists two actions: the news first, then your typed request.

💬 Example: type `what's the weather today` as the custom action.

## Step 6 — Save and test it
Tap **Save**. Now walk over to your Echo and say **"Alexa, good morning."** Alexa should play the news and then tell you the weather. If nothing happens, open the routine again and check the phrase for typos, and make sure the routine is set to run on the device you're talking to.
You'll know it worked when Alexa runs both actions after your phrase.

💬 Example: say `Alexa, good morning` to your Echo.

## Common mistakes
- **Typing "Alexa" into the phrase:** the phrase is only what comes after the wake word. Type `good morning`, then say "Alexa, good morning".
- **Putting the custom action first:** Amazon's help says custom actions need to be the last action in a routine. Move it to the end.
- **Expecting a device you haven't connected:** a smart-home or music action only works with devices and services already added to the Alexa app.

## What this means for you
- **In everyday life:** One phrase in the morning gets you the news and the weather while you make coffee — no tapping, no scrolling.
- **For your business or work:** In a home office, a "start work" routine can read your calendar and switch on a compatible desk lamp.
- **If you're just getting started:** Begin with a single spoken phrase and one action. Once it works, add more actions — and remember to keep any custom action last.

## Try it now
Open the Alexa app, tap **More** → **Routines** → **+**, add the event phrase **test routine**, add a custom action that says **tell me a joke**, and tap **Save**. Then say "Alexa, test routine" — you'll have a working routine in about two minutes.
